EXPLANATION: The spectrum is dominated by aliphatic C–H stretches at 2946 / 2887 cm⁻¹ and a strong CH₂/CH₃ deformation at 1450 cm⁻¹, indicating a purely aliphatic molecule.  
Triethylamine (CCN(CC)CC) is known to show:

• a very strong C–N stretch near 1065 cm⁻¹ – matching the 1057 cm⁻¹ peak (and the weaker 1079 cm⁻¹ companion).  
• CH₃/CH₂ rocking-type skeletal modes near 920 cm⁻¹ (observed 919 cm⁻¹) and near 820 cm⁻¹ (observed 831 cm⁻¹).  
• Additional low-frequency C–C skeletal bands around 740-780 cm⁻¹ (observed 771 cm⁻¹).  

No bands are seen in the 2100–2200 cm⁻¹ (Si-H) or 2300–2400 cm⁻¹ (N≡N, S-H, P-H) regions, ruling out silicon-containing or azide/diazo candidates.  
The presence of two characteristic C–O stretches expected for ethers (~1050 & 1150 cm⁻¹) is not required, making the ether and thioether candidates less consistent.

Overall, the pattern of CH stretches, a single strong C–N stretch, and the specific skeletal bands at 919/831/771 cm⁻¹ best fits triethylamine.
